newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-INDIANS PLACE JUSTICE AND OGEA ON DISABLED LIST.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-INDIANS PLACE JUSTICE AND OGEA ON DISABLED LIST.

text.p: The Cleveland Indians Tuesday were forced to place star left fielder David Justice and right handed pitcher Chad Ogea on the 15-day disabled list.
Justice sat out four games after hyperextending his left elbow against the Cardinals June 14 and went 1-for-9 when he tried to work his way back as a designated hitter last weekend.
After his weekend struggles, the Indians, who are in first place in the American League Central Division, decided to place Justice on the DL, retroactive to Monday.

Justice, who was acquired from Atlanta along with outfielder Marquis Grissom for Kenny Lofton in a blockbuster deal during spring training, is hitting .344 with 10 homers, 20 doubles, 34 RBI and 34 runs scored. He is second in the league to Frank Thomas with a .665 slugging percentage.
Ironically, the Braves were forced to place Lofton on the disabled list Monday.
Ogea, who suffered his fifth consecutive defeat Monday to to Minnesota, has a strained right elbow. Ogea is 0-5 in June with a 7.52 ERA.
Overall, he is 5-7 with a 5.56 ERA this season and has allowed 99 hits in 92.1 innings, striking out 61.
